The Superclásico That Brings Argentina to a Standstill: Here’s How Boca and River Are Heading to La Bombonera
Lluvia Zazueta 
 · 
 Oct 31, 2026 
 · 
 3 min read 
 FM FANS 
 World Soccer.— This Sunday, November 1, the classic match that brings Argentina—and much of the soccer world—to a standstill will take place: Boca Juniors and River Plate will face off at La Bombonera at 3:00 p.m. Argentina time, 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time, and 11:00 a.m. Pacific Time, broadcast on ViX and Fubo in the United States. It’s the 267th El Clásico, on Matchday 15 of the Clausura Tournament, and both teams are in good form, though with different priorities.
 Boca is playing at home and riding a wave of high spirits. According to the results from Matchday 14, the Xeneize have won their last three league matches: 3-0 against Unión at La Bombonera, 2-1 against Talleres also at home, and 1-0 against Independiente in Avellaneda, with a goal by Facundo Herrera. With 27 points—the result of seven wins, six draws, and just one loss—Boca sits third in Group A, five points behind the leader, and has already secured its spot in the round of 16.
 But Boca’s main motivation lies on the international stage. As reported following the semifinal, Rodolfo Arruabarrena’s team is a finalist in the Copa Sudamericana: they lost the first leg 1-0 to Vasco da Gama at La Bombonera, but came back with a 3-1 victory at the Maracanã, with goals from Lautaro Di Lollo, Miguel Merentiel, and a late strike by Leandro Paredes, for a 3-2 aggregate win. The final will be held on November 21 in Barranquilla against Atlético Mineiro, and the winner will take home $10 million and a spot in the 2027 Copa Libertadores. In addition, Boca remains in contention in the Copa Argentina, where it will face Banfield in the semifinals. In other words, the Xeneize heads into the Superclásico competing on three fronts.
 River, on the other hand, needs to secure its qualification. According to pre-match reports, El Millonario is fourth in Group B with 23 points—seven wins, two draws, and five losses—and has not yet secured its spot in the round of 16. Their current form, however, is solid: they beat Racing 1-0 at the Monumental on Matchday 14, thrashed Belgrano 3-0 in Córdoba, and drew 1-1 with Sarmiento—for three wins in their last four matches.
 Recent history favors the home team: the last Superclásico, on April 19, 2026, at the Monumental, was won by Boca 1-0 on a penalty kick by Leandro Paredes. And in the annual standings, which determine qualification for the 2027 cup competitions, Boca leads with 57 points, while River is seventh with 52, so Sunday’s result will also impact that race.
 One key development to watch in this away match: Lucas Martínez Quarta returns after serving a suspension against Racing for accumulating yellow cards—a suspension he deliberately sought to ensure he’d be available for the Superclásico—and is set to partner Nicolás Otamendi in central defense.
 The match will be refereed by Nicolás Ramírez, with Silvio Trucco on VAR.
 With La Bombonera as the setting, Boca as a continental finalist, and River needing a win to avoid complicating its qualification, Sunday’s Superclásico has all the ingredients to bring Argentine soccer to a standstill.

Lluvia Zazueta
